title: Datary: local-first terminal laboratory for reproducible program and simulation evidence
description:
Overview

Datary is a local-first terminal laboratory for recording, validating, analysing, replaying, comparing, plotting, and reporting evidence emitted by programs and simulations. It preserves original input alongside accepted and invalid records, records assumptions and measurements, and keeps input inert rather than executing it.

Key capabilities

  • Disk-backed, bounded recording of CSV, TSV, JSON, JSON Lines, streams, and key-value rows.
  • Deterministic metrics, heuristic quality checks, integrity verification, experiment comparison, replay, plotting, and Markdown or JSON reports.
  • Typed Python API and deterministic synthetic profiles for reproducible demonstrations.

Install

python -m pip install https://github.com/devkyato/Datary/releases/download/v0.2.4/datary_lab-0.2.4-py3-none-any.whl
datary --version

Quick start

datary generate noisy-sensor --seed 1 --output noisy.jsonl
datary inspect noisy.jsonl --time-field timestamp --quality

Applications

  • Recording and comparing numerical simulation runs.
  • Validating embedded-device telemetry.
  • Teaching reproducible data analysis in student laboratories.
  • Preserving local engineering and coursework evidence.

Limitations/status

Version 0.2.4 is alpha software. Datary does not authenticate authorship, infer physical-unit conversions, interpolate comparison series, choose domain thresholds, or establish scientific validity. Checksums detect accidental corruption but are not signatures.

Documentation

Start with the documentation index, then read the reproducibility boundaries and security policy.

Related software

  • OpenNet for typed embedded-to-host messaging.
  • Lowpack for local-first application-aware packing.
  • Relay for timing-risk source review.
